fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. Eliphaz, one of Job's three friends, calls Job's talk “empty counsel” and asks if a wise man would fill his belly with “…the hot east wind?” (Job 15:2). Neither of those sounds gentle. He is calling the words empty, and I'd hate to get that review on a batch.

That's the one, baker. Eliphaz says, “Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.” (Job 15:6). He is pointing at what Job has said. Mouth and lips both do the testifying, so Job's own words are the witness here.

Feet are a nice guess, baker, but they stay out of this one. Eliphaz says, “Your own mouth, not mine, condemns you; your own lips testify against you.” (Job 15:6). Mouth and lips are both about talking, so the answer is mouth. My own feet are stuck to a gold base, so I'm not getting blamed for anything either!

Other way around, friend. Eliphaz says the gray-haired and the aged are on their side, “…men much older than your father.” (Job 15:10). Those elders are the ones he says are older than Job's father. So that answer doesn't match what Eliphaz says.

Praying isn't what Eliphaz brings up here, baker. He asks, “Do you listen in on the council of God or limit wisdom to yourself?” (Job 15:8). Then he asks, “What do you know that we do not?” (Job 15:9). Eliphaz is asking whether Job has some wisdom the rest of them don't, and prayer never enters into it.

It's true, friend. Eliphaz says, “Both the gray-haired and the aged are on our side—men much older than your father.” (Job 15:10). So the elders he mentions are older than Job's own father. He is not saying they're younger or the same age. I think he wants Job to feel how many experienced voices agree with him.

Hiding isn't what Eliphaz says, friend. He asks why Job's heart has carried him away and why his eyes flash, “…so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?” (Job 15:12-13). The charge is turning his spirit against God and pouring out words. Hiding his face never comes up.

Running away isn't what Eliphaz says, baker. He asks why Job's heart has carried him away and why his eyes flash, “…so that you turn your spirit against God and pour such words from your mouth?” (Job 15:12-13). The accusation is that Job turns his spirit against God. Running from Him isn't in the verse.

That's it, baker. Eliphaz says man is “…vile and corrupt, who drinks injustice like water?” (Job 15:16). Water is something people drink all the time, so that's a picture of injustice going down easy. It's a heavy way for Eliphaz to talk about people.

Servants don't show up in this verse, baker. Eliphaz says the wicked man “…has stretched out his hand against God and has vaunted himself against the Almighty…” (Job 15:25). The reason he gives is about how the man stands toward God. I'd say that one gets the whole spotlight.

It's true, friend. Eliphaz says the wicked man is “…rushing headlong at Him with a thick, studded shield.” (Job 15:26). That's a man charging at God with a heavy shield out front. Picture that full-speed run and you've got the verse.

Holy is a good word, baker, but it isn't this one. Eliphaz says the wicked man “…will dwell in ruined cities, in abandoned houses destined to become rubble.” (Job 15:28). The places are ruined and abandoned, and the word on the card is ruined.

That's right, friend. Eliphaz says, “He will no longer be rich; his wealth will not endure. His possessions will not overspread the land.” (Job 15:29). So the wealth won't last, and his possessions won't spread across the land. That's why the statement is false.

That's his point, baker. Eliphaz says, “…his branch will not flourish.” and then pictures “…a vine stripped of its unripe grapes…” and “…an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.” (Job 15:32-33). Both pictures show something losing what it was growing. That's the image he gives of the wicked man.

Feeding folks isn't the picture, baker. Eliphaz says, “…his branch will not flourish.” and then points to a vine stripped of its unripe grapes and an olive tree that sheds its blossoms (Job 15:32-33). Those are pictures of losing what was growing. Nothing in them is about a big harvest or feeding anyone.
